definition: EEG biofeedback, also called neurofeedback, is a method being studied to improve brain function by showing a person their brain activity on a computer using sensors placed on the head. Sounds such as beeps or tones may be used as rewards when the person changes certain patterns of brain activity, and it may help with stress and mental side effects in some medical contexts.
